issues.detail: The Hebrew 'עִירָא הַיָּאִרִי' means 'Ira the Jairite' (a gentilic from Jair, a clan/family name). The Chinese renders it as '以拉人，就是雅伊人' which reads as 'the Irite, that is, the Jairite' — treating 'Ira' as a place/people name and 'Jairite' as an appositive. This misidentifies the proper name 'Ira' (a person) as a gentilic, and mislabels the Jairite as a separate identity rather than the same person's clan designation. A reader would understand two different groups/identities instead of one person, Ira the Jairite.
